description.content:
Teel's partner-facing REST API. Partners authenticate with `sk_live_*`
(production) or `sk_test_*` (sandbox) bearer tokens issued by Teel.
See the [Authentication guide](https://docs.teel.finance/authentication)
for key issuance, rotation, and revocation.

**Conventions:**
- All endpoints accept and return JSON. Request bodies must set
  `Content-Type: application/json`.
- All money amounts use truncation (never rounding). Stablecoin
  precision is 6 dp; fiat is 2 dp.
- Write endpoints accept `Idempotency-Key: <8-255 url-safe chars>` for
  Stripe-style retry deduplication (24h window).
- List endpoints accept `?limit` and `?offset` for pagination. Limits
  are clamped to a per-endpoint maximum.
- Errors use `application/json` with `{ "code": "<CODE>", "error":
  "<message>" }`. The `code` is the stable, machine-readable identifier
  partners should switch on; `error` is human-readable and may change.


Contact Support:
 Name: Teel API team
 Email: api@teel.finance

Unauthenticated. Returns `200` and `{ "status": "ok", "env": "<APP_ENV>" }`
whenever the API process is running. Use this on the partner side to
distinguish a Teel-side outage from a partner-side credential bug.
Unauthenticated. Use for client codegen / Postman import.

item.name: Lock a quote and execute a payout

description.content:
Lock-and-execute: this single call generates a quote from
`(fromCurrency, toCurrency, amount, recipientId)`, locks it, and
starts the payout. There is no separate `/quotes/*` → `/rfq/execute`
two-step. Pass `routeProtocol` from a `/quotes/*` response if you
want to pin a specific route token; otherwise the engine selects
the best route at lock time.

Scope: `payouts:write`. Idempotent via `Idempotency-Key`. The
response is wrapped in `{success, data}` — the partner-visible
payload sits on `data`.

Optional. Stripe-style idempotency: same key + same body → cached
response replayed within 24h with `Idempotency-Replayed: true`.
Same key + different body → 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED. Concurrent
in-flight → 409 IDEMPOTENCY_REQUEST_IN_FLIGHT + Retry-After.

item.name: Lock and execute a batch of payouts

description.content:
Same lock-and-execute model as `POST /rfq/execute`, but for N
payouts that share a source `fromCurrency` and (optionally) a
single funding `userPaymentMethodId`. The per-row envelope is
keyed by `idx` so partial failure is graceful — walk
`data.rows[]`, retry the `retryable:true` failures with the
same row-level `idempotency_key`.

Scope: `payouts:write`. Idempotent via `Idempotency-Key` for the
envelope; per-row dedup uses `items[].idempotency_key`.

Optional. Stripe-style idempotency: same key + same body → cached
response replayed within 24h with `Idempotency-Replayed: true`.
Same key + different body → 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED. Concurrent
in-flight → 409 IDEMPOTENCY_REQUEST_IN_FLIGHT + Retry-After.

request.name: Lock and execute a batch of payouts

description.content:
For stablecoin-to-fiat payouts, your wallet sends the source
stablecoin to the `escrowAddress` returned by `/rfq/execute`.
The engine auto-detects the deposit via on-chain log polling.
If detection misses your transfer — slow chain, late tx, dropped
log — call this endpoint with the tx hash to register the
deposit manually. The offramp leg proceeds as soon as the on-chain
amount and destination are verified.

Scope: `payouts:write`. Idempotent: re-submitting the same
`quoteId` + `txHash` after the deposit is already confirmed
returns `{success: true}` again.

Optional. Stripe-style idempotency: same key + same body → cached
response replayed within 24h with `Idempotency-Replayed: true`.
Same key + different body → 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED. Concurrent
in-flight → 409 IDEMPOTENCY_REQUEST_IN_FLIGHT + Retry-After.

item.name: Get the current status of a payout / locked quote

description.content:
Lookup by the `quoteId` returned from `/rfq/execute` (or any
successful row of `/rfq/execute-batch`). Response is wrapped in
`{success, data}`.

Scope: `payouts:read`. For push-based updates use the webhook
events `payout.status.updated` / `payout.delivered` instead of
polling.

item.name: Get the merged field schema for creating recipients

description.content:
Returns the merged field schema partners use to build a dynamic
recipient-create form. Provider-specific quirks are unioned into
a single flat shape with two type-specific sections (`bank` and
`wallet`). Provider names are not exposed in the response — the
merge layer strips them.

Scope: `recipients:read`. Scoped to the authenticated partner's
live provider accounts.
